clue.text: Message from Sky when A&E show suffers power cut

parts.note: A&E, the hospital's Accident and Emergency department, is written AE

indicators.note: cut says the power letter is cut out of the show word

parts.note: a show on TV is a programme
P is the standard symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A hospital TV series suffers a blackout and a message about it comes from the Sky broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the satellite TV company, fitting the show and power cut, but here it is simply the sky, the route an airmail letter takes. 'cut' removes P from PROGRAMME, leaving ROGRAMME.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerogramme is a lightweight airmail letter, so it is a message sent by air, through the sky.

clue.text: Deep-voiced female singer in Toto? Get her to quit!

indicators.note: to quit says the letters of get her leave the longer word

parts.note: in toto is Latin for wholly, which is altogether
the words get her are taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with a contralto in the band Toto wants her to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toto' looks like the rock band, but 'in Toto' is the Latin phrase meaning ALTOGETHER; 'to quit' takes GETHER out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is the lowest female singing voice, so the singer with that voice is deep-voiced.

clue.text: If you clipped all of grey car's fender, driver in front would be ____-_____

definitions.text: If you clipped all of grey car's fender, driver in front would be ____-_____

indicators.note: clipped all of says each of these words loses its outside letters at both ends
in front says only the leading letter of driver is used

explanation.surface: If you dented the whole of a grey car's bumper, the driver ahead would have been hit from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped all of' trims both ends of each of grey, car's and fender; 'in front' takes the opening letter of driver. The whole clue is also the scene: clip the car ahead and it is struck from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that is rear-ended is struck from behind by the vehicle following it, as when you clip its bumper.

clue.text: Fertiliser that's good for minute valley

indicators.note: good for minute says the letter for good stands in for the letter for minute

parts.note: mulch is a layer of organic matter spread to feed and protect soil

explanation.surface: A gardener praises a fertiliser that works wonders on a tiny valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like an adjective meaning tiny, describing the valley, but it is M, the abbreviation for a minute of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow steep-sided ravine, a kind of valley in American usage.

clue.text: Answer question the setter's rejected at first as poorly composed

parts.note: the setter's means the setter has, which from the setter's own mouth is I've

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of rejected is taken

explanation.surface: A setter's answer to a question was turned down for being badly written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the setter's' stands for 'the setter has', which the setter would say as I'VE. 'poorly composed' looks like a verdict on writing, but it means not composed, in a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquiver means trembling with nerves or excitement, the opposite of being calm and collected.

clue.text: Pen in support of form and decency

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece in support of another sits beneath it

parts.note: a mode is a form or manner of something
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A pen is used to back up both a document form and propriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is propriety in dress and behaviour, the quality of being decent and not showing off.

clue.text: After retiring, President died

parts.note: Abe, short for Abraham Lincoln, is a common crossword president
D is the usual abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A president died after stepping down from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like leaving a job, which suits a president, but it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to bed, so someone who has retired for the night is in bed.

clue.text: From the outset, besotted Romeo adored virtues of Juliet?

indicators.note: from the outset says the opening letters of the next five words are used

explanation.surface: Smitten Romeo worshipped Juliet's virtues right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juliet' looks like Shakespeare's heroine, but the question mark points to Juliet Bravo, a 1980s BBC police drama; Juliet and Bravo are also neighbouring words in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet Bravo was the title of a British TV police series, so this word completes the name Juliet.

clue.text: The way to make sea sprats in grapeseed for starter?

definitions.text: The way to make sea sprats in grapeseed for starter?

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
fry are young or small fish, such as sprats

indicators.note: for starter says only the first letter of grapeseed is used

explanation.surface: A recipe question: how to cook little sea fish in grapeseed oil as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like the first course of a meal but asks for the opening letter, G. The whole clue also describes the cooking: sprats plunged into grapeseed oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-frying cooks food fully immersed in hot oil, a usual way to cook small fish such as sprats.

clue.text: Peevishly incarcerating leader of Persians in Tyre

indicators.note: incarcerating means locking up, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: to act crossly is to act peevishly or irritably

indicators.note: leader of says only the first letter of Persians is taken

explanation.surface: Someone grumpily imprisons a Persian chief in the ancient city of Tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tyre' looks like the Phoenician city, which suits Persians, but it is a car tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-ply is a type of tyre whose internal cords run diagonally across each other.

clue.text: Vacuous troll barracking immature use of Net

indicators.note: barracking means housing as if in barracks, so the first piece encloses the second
vacuous means empty, so troll keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: raw means inexperienced or immature

explanation.surface: An empty-headed internet troll heckles someone over their childish online behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barracking' looks like heckling, which suits a troll, but it means putting up in barracks. 'Net' looks like the internet; it is a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: A trawl is the act of fishing by dragging a wide net along behind a boat.

clue.text: Promise to go with you to the grave, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to pledge or promise to do something

definitions.text: to go with you to the grave, perhaps
definitions.meaning: the sense here is to act as ..., the person who handles a funeral and takes you to the grave

explanation.surface: A vow to stay with someone until death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one loving promise; split it, and the second half is the job of an undertaker, with 'perhaps' warning that the sense is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake is to commit to a task; it also playfully means doing an undertaker's funeral work.

clue.text: 75 per cent of brewer's output facing rash cuts ahead

indicators.note: 75 per cent of keeps three of the four letters of the brewer's product, dropping the last

parts.note: a brewer makes beer
hives is an itchy skin rash

explanation.surface: A brewery boss facing a rash of cutbacks is told three-quarters of output must go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' looks like spending cuts, but it means haircuts, and 'ahead' places them on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive is a tall, rounded hairstyle, so it is a cut worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Viz not usual standard fare

parts.note: viz and sc (scilicet) are both Latin abbreviations meaning namely
food that is off is below its usual standard, having gone bad

explanation.surface: The comic Viz is not up to its usual standard of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viz' looks like the British adult comic, but it is the abbreviation meaning namely, here swapped for its twin SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff is British slang for food, which is what fare means in a meal sense.

clue.text: Dessert wine that may cause rumbling down below later

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the course after the main meal
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A dessert wine that might upset the stomach afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumbling down below' looks like an upset stomach after dessert wine, but it means a tremor deep in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftershock is a smaller tremor following an earthquake, so it is a later underground rumble.

clue.text: Office worker lodges religious don who's scraping to get by?

indicators.note: lodges means gives lodging to, so the first piece houses the second

parts.note: a filer is an office clerk who files documents
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a university religious scholar

explanation.surface: An office clerk takes in a lodger, a theology academic barely making ends meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraping to get by' looks like struggling for money, but it describes drawing a bow across a violin, with a hint at fiddling to survive.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the violin by scraping the bow, and a fiddler is also a cheat living on small dodges.

clue.text: Exotic Asian lot?

indicators.note: exotic means strange or out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A group of people from Asia, seen as exotic.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of ASIAN LOT make a people who are themselves an Asian lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Laotians are the people of Laos in Southeast Asia, so they are indeed a group of Asians.

clue.text: Lift status: ascent quiet if maintained within two years

indicators.note: maintained within means held inside, so the year letters wrap the rest

parts.note: Y is the usual abbreviation for year, so two years give two of them
an ascent is a going up
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Instructions about a lift's status: it went up quietly, if kept running for two years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like an elevator, which suits ascent, but it is a verb meaning raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To yuppify an area is to gentrify it, raising its social standing with young professionals.

clue.text: Scared witless, I'd gone — made me think

indicators.note: gone says those letters disappear from the longer word

parts.note: to be intimidated is to be frightened, scared out of one's wits
I'd is taken letter for letter, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone frightened out of their wits by a disappearance ponders it.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to hint or suggest, so something intimated made a person think it without saying it.

clue.text: Last documents to be shredded after copper's gone

indicators.note: shredding cuts paper into scraps, so the letters are reassembled in a new order
gone says the copper letters leave the pool before it makes the answer

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: The final documents are shredded once the police officer has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, which suits shredding documents, but it is the metal, symbol CU. The letters of DOCUMENTS make the answer plus CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest towards the end, so the endmost item is the final one in a row.

clue.text: Dull, sort of like pool?

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake or pool
-ish is a suffix meaning sort of, or somewhat like

explanation.surface: A question whether something is boring, a bit like a still pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish metal is to dull its shine, as when silver loses its lustre.

clue.text: Skipping regularly, Kirby exercises leg, producing gas

indicators.note: skipping regularly means every other letter of Kirby is jumped over

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercises
on is the leg side in cricket, the side where the batsman stands

explanation.surface: Someone called Kirby skips rope and does leg exercises, then gives off wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipping' looks like the exercise, but it means omitting letters. 'leg' is ON, the cricket term for the leg side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is a noble gas, an element used in some lighting.

clue.text: Behaving like Jack, King and Queen in service

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: in says the Queen letters go inside the service word

parts.note: the navy is one of the armed services
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Playing cards: a Jack behaves like a King and Queen serving together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a playing card beside King and Queen, but here a jack is a rogue or knave.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack in cards is also called the knave, and knavery is dishonest, roguish conduct.

clue.text: Japanese consumers love this piece of inglorious US history

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Japan enjoys a shameful part of American history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumers' looks like shoppers, but it means people who eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi, vinegared rice with raw fish, is a dish hugely popular with people who eat in Japan.

clue.text: Thereafter car company fails to get foreign capital

parts.note: so can mean then or thereafter, as in 'and so to bed'

indicators.note: fails here means the car company falls short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Fiat is the Italian car maker

explanation.surface: A car manufacturer later fails to win a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' is a loose deletion signal: FIAT falls short by its last letter, T, giving FIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria, so it is a capital abroad.

clue.text: Content of family tree is wrong, as it happens

indicators.note: is wrong means the letters are put in an incorrect, scrambled order
the content of a word is what sits inside it, its letters minus the ends

explanation.surface: A genealogist complains that what is written in a family tree is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content of' takes the inside of family, which 'is wrong' scrambles with tree. 'as it happens' looks like 'incidentally' but means live, at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in real time takes place live, at the moment events occur.

clue.text: When cycling, criticise noiseless wheels

indicators.note: cycling means letters are rotated round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: to slate is to criticise severely

explanation.surface: A cyclist complains about wheels that make no sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When cycling' moves TE from the end of SLATE to the front. 'wheels' looks like bicycle wheels, but it is slang for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tesla is an electric car, near silent when running, and wheels is slang for a car.

clue.text: Tat fringe on jumper during work time

indicators.note: during means within, so the edge letter sits inside the work word

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: fringe on means the edge letter of jumper, here the final one

explanation.surface: Someone sews a fringe onto a cheap sweater while at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a sweater, and its fringe here is its last letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Grot is British slang for rubbish or junk, which is what tat means.

clue.text: Charge with indecency

definitions.meaning: a military charge or attack, a noun
the adjective sense: indecent or giving offence

explanation.surface: A legal accusation of indecent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an accusation in court, but it is a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is an attacking campaign, while offensive as an adjective means insulting or improper.

clue.text: Lech Walesa's last letter hampers quiet youngster superficially

indicators.note: hampers means hinders by getting in the way, so the letter sits inside the quiet word

parts.note: st is the hushing sound asking for quiet

indicators.note: last letter says only the final letter of Walesa is taken
superficially means only on the surface, so youngster keeps just its outer letters

explanation.surface: Lech Walesa's final letter is held up while a youth is treated shallowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lech' looks like the first name of Walesa, the Polish leader, but it is the definition: a lecher.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful man, after the goatish woodland gods of Greek myth, so he is a lech.

clue.text: Met governor, one originally from Asia

definitions.meaning: Sadiq ..., as Mayor of London, oversees the Metropolitan Police, the Met
a ruler or governor in Central Asia, the original holders of the title

explanation.surface: A London official whose family came from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is London's Metropolitan Police, overseen by the Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: Khan is the surname of London's mayor and also the title of Mongol and Central Asian rulers.

clue.text: Day One, Two, Three … could be start of original new version of this?

definitions.text: Day One, Two, Three … could be start of original new version of this?

indicators.note: could be says these words might turn into something else once their letters are rearranged
a new version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged
start of says only the first letter of original is taken

explanation.surface: A countdown of days might be how a remake of the beginning starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DAY ONE TWO THREE are the answer plus O (start of 'original') and NEW: 'could be' and 'version of' tell you to rearrange them. Counting up from day one also takes you back to the earliest time.
explanation.definitionFit: The year dot is a British phrase for the very distant past, as if at the start of the calendar.
